text_span: The accurate estimation of catastrophe tail risk—specifically Value at Risk (VaR) and Tail Value at Risk (TVaR) at extreme percentiles—poses a profound computational challenge
rationale: States the central problem motivating the paper.

text_span: Traditional classical Monte Carlo (MC) simulations suffer from high estimator variance and severe sample inefficiency when modeling low-probability, high-severity events.
rationale: Identifies a key limitation of the classical baseline.

text_span: we introduce a hybrid quantum-classical simulation architecture designed to reduce estimator variance and optimize non-proportional reinsurance layer structures.
rationale: Summarizes the paper’s main proposed system.

text_span: Our system integrates physics-based classical catastrophe modeling with Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) and Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQE)
rationale: Specifies the quantum methods used in the architecture.

text_span: our system introduces a dynamic backend scheduler driven by a multi-variable scoring function balancing precision, queue latency, and cost, alongside Zero-Noise Extrapolation (ZNE) for error mitigation.
rationale: Highlights operational scheduling and error-mitigation design choices.
